objective: One diagnosis arm for the S1 floating-point-exception crash class that has now hit the k-family closures in two geometries: the bump at high Re within about 45 iterations and the hills kEpsilon at iteration 13
rationale: Family B's re1p2e7 group lost kEpsilon, kOmegaSST and realizableKE to sigFpe crashes within about 45 iterations, and family H's kEpsilon died the same S1 death at iteration 13 on a fully compliant mesh where kOmegaSST converges cleanly. Two geometries, one crash signature, and one shared construction: both families carry this batch's derived-epsilon pieces -- an epsilon field built from Cmu k omega with epsilonWallFunction lowReCorrection on wall-resolved grids -- which makes a single root cause plausible and worth one arm rather than two. What a SHARED root cause would look like, stated in advance: the FPE traceback names the same equation and the same region in both geometries (the epsilon or k equation at wall-adjacent or freestream-boundary cells, a division on collapsing k or epsilon), and one lever -- seeding epsilon from the converged same-case kOmegaSST field's k and omega instead of the uniform derivation, or an epsilonMin floor -- removes the crash in BOTH. What geometry-specific causes would look like: tracebacks naming different equations or stages (the hills' meanVelocityForce interplay at iteration 13 versus the bump's high-Re freestream scaling at 45), or a lever that fixes one geometry and not the other. Either answer routes the batch's k-family coverage: shared means one initialization fix re-opens four dead cells across two families; specific means the exclusions are case physics and stand. The arm inherits review entry 9's per-quantity settle-monitoring design: every probe writes per-iteration min and max of k, epsilon and nut beside the residuals, so the collapse is watched in the quantity, not inferred from the crash line.
gate: Deliverable is the named crash mechanism per geometry with the runtime evidence attached: the sigFpe traceback or last-iteration field state, the per-quantity min-max history to the crash, the shared-vs-specific verdict against the two pre-stated signatures, and one lever arm per geometry with its outcome. Per L-40, any lever cited as tested carries the runtime-log line proving it was active. No band changes and no member admissions flow from this arm; a rescued cell re-enters only through the standing gate under its own record
cost_basis: measured where it can be: the crashes themselves cost 0.04 to 0.07 core-min each to reproduce, the instrumented probes are the same seconds-scale runs with monitoring on, and the priced bulk is the two lever arms if they survive to run -- family H's kEpsilon at the measured 7 core-min class and one bump cell at the measured 2.3 core-min class, with margin
expected_knowledge_gain: Either one initialization defect explains four dead cells across two families and the k-family coverage of the standing batch re-opens for the cost of a seeding change, or the crash class is shown geometry-specific and the exclusions harden into case findings. Both outcomes also hand the monitor standard a worked example of per-quantity crash forensics on the S1 class

The monitoring named two different roads to one death site: hills kEpsilon's turbulence fields explode globally from the uniform derived initialization (min epsilon 4.96e+45, max nut 2.4e+153, viscosity-locked U) while the bump diverges locally in momentum from the impulsive uniform start at the 20x Reynolds step (max U 9.4e+22 near-wall aft-bump). Both levers removed their crashes: SST-seeded per-cell k/epsilon survived 3000 iterations on the hills, potentialFoam init survived 2000 on the bump.
